The relationships between these equilibrium constants are as follows:

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Each partial pressure is p = (n / N) × P, so equation (7) should be Kp = Kn (P/N)^Δn. The printed Kp = Kn (N)^Δn leaves out the total pressure P.
Where:
R = General gas constant
T = Absolute temperature of the system
P = Pressure of the system
N = Total number of moles of reactants and products
Δn = Difference of number of moles of products and reactants in the balanced chemical equation

It depends upon the value of ‘Δn’ that which of the equilibrium constants is bigger or smaller than the other. Anyhow, if the number of moles of reactants and products in a balanced chemical equation are equal, and all the constants have equal values. That is,

blocks.text_alt: Δn = 0 then Kp = Kc = Kx = Kn

blocks.text: Hence, whichever concentration units are used, the equilibrium constants are same.
Sample Problem 8.3
N₂(g) and H₂(g) combine to form NH₃(g). The value of Kc at 500 °C is 6.0 × 10⁻². Calculate the numerical value of Kp for this reaction.
bold: N₂(g) and H₂(g) combine to form NH₃(g). The value of Kc at 500 °C is 6.0 × 10⁻². Calculate the numerical value of Kp for this reaction.

blocks.text: Solution:
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)
R = 0.0821 dm³ atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹
Kp = ?
The formula for conversion of Kc to Kp is,
Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn
Δn = Number of moles of product − Number of moles of reactants
Substituting these values in the expression:
Kp = 6.0 × 10⁻² (0.0821 dm³ atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ × 773 K)⁻²
= 6.0 × 10⁻² (63.5 dm³ atm mol⁻¹)⁻²
So, the value of Kp is less than Kc.

Sample Problem 8.4
In the reaction
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)
the equilibrium partial pressures at constant temperature are SO₂ = 1.0 × 10⁶ Pa, O₂ = 7.0 × 10⁶ Pa, SO₃ = 8.0 × 10⁶ Pa. Calculate the value of Kp for this reaction.
Solution
Step 1 Write the equilibrium expression for the reaction in terms of partial pressures.
Kp = P²SO₃ / P²SO₂ × PO₂
Step 2 Substitute the equilibrium concentrations into the expression.
Kp = 9.1 × 10⁻⁶ Pa⁻¹
Quick Check 8.5

blocks.prompt:
a) Decide the comparative magnitudes of Kc and Kp, for the following reversible reactions.
1. Ammonia synthesis
2. Dissociation of PCl₅
blocks.explanation: Ammonia synthesis (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃): Δn = −2, so Kp = Kc (RT)⁻², i.e. Kp is smaller than Kc. PCl₅ ⇌ PCl₃ + Cl₂: Δn = +1, so Kp = Kc × RT, i.e. Kp is larger than Kc.
